systems.name: creative-core
systems.description: The pure-Swift engines of a Mac-native creative suite: the FlareCore animation engine plus the shared CoreColor, CoreRaster, CoreAsset, CoreCatalog, CoreRender and CoreRenderMetal modules. Linux-safe, Foundation only, except CoreCatalog, which uses GRDB over the system SQLite, and CoreRenderMetal, which uses Metal on macOS and builds empty on Linux. The Mac apps live in other repos.

containers.name: FlareCore library
containers.description: The FlareCore Swift package (Sources/FlareCore). Value types only, Codable and Sendable, and nothing crashes on untrusted input.

components.name: Document and Command Engine
components.description: The document model (Document > Scene > Layer > Shape, keyframe tracks, fills, text shapes, ruler guides, the W1 layer masks and track mattes, text runs with paragraph and path-text styles and their text layout, colour and shape tracks, the swatch palette, metadata, frame labels) and its ModelError; LayerOwner, which addresses a scene's or a symbol's layer list; the Command protocol and CommandEngine with exact undo/redo, groups, coalescing, an undo depth limit and layer-scoped validation for single-layer commands; the CommandRegistry that decodes any command from a JSON envelope; the built-in command families (scene, layer, shape, text, keyframe, label, guide, swatch, metadata), with the stroke, path and duplicate-layer commands, scene canvas, rename and reorder; and the .flare v1 file format with validation. Every document change goes through a Command.

components.name: Geometry
components.description: 2D affine Matrix, the Transform (position, scale, rotation; scene space is y down) layers and instances use, axis-aligned Rect, vector Paths with line, quadratic and cubic segments and their affine transform, tight shape bounds, and point hit testing (even-odd and nonzero fill, strokes, through instances). The per-frame render list of a scene or symbol: one walk that gives the layer and instance tree exporters write and the flat paint-order items (matrix, multiplied opacity, inherited lock, address) the stage draws; the queries over it (topmost hit with a tolerance, marquee, world bounds with stroke); and the path builders for rectangles, ellipses, polygons and stars. Nothing here traps on non-finite input.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: Frame/time conversion, keyframe interpolation with binary-search segment lookup, easing curves (linear, cubic bezier, hold), sampling a layer's property values (and its colour and shape tracks) at a frame for rendering and export, and onion skin frames around the playhead.

components.name: Export
components.description: Exporters that turn a scene into other formats: one frame as an SVG document, a scene as a Lottie JSON document with animated position, scale, rotation and opacity, and gradient stop alpha, and the frame plan (numbers, times, pixel sizes, file names) for a numbered PNG sequence. Output is byte-stable and throws on non-finite values. W1 writers fill one seam file each: SVGExporter+Style (paint at the frame), SVGExporter+Text (text runs), SVGExporter+Masks and LottieExporter+Masks (layer masks and track mattes), LottieExporter+Tracks (animated properties, including colour, width and shape keys).

components.name: Import
components.description: Importers that read the vector formats export writes, its inverse: the contract for an SVG document read into one scene and a Lottie JSON document read into a document, with byte, element, layer and depth caps, a typed ImportError and an ImportReport listing what was skipped; SVGPathData, which reads SVG path data (every command, absolute and relative, arcs as cubics) into a Path; and XMLTokens, the bounded, Linux-safe XML tokenizer the SVG reader walks (tags, attributes, text, entities; comments, declarations and CDATA skipped). The Lottie reader turns shape and solid layers, their paths, rectangles, ellipses, fills, strokes, gradients and transforms into one scene, with keyframes (easings from the file's handles, holds) as position, scale, rotation, opacity, colour, stroke width and shape tracks, masks as layer masks and tt as track mattes, counting parents, expressions, keyed anchors and group transforms and other layer kinds as skipped; the SVG document reader turns basic shapes and paths, with their transforms baked in, solid and gradient fills (href chains followed with a visited set), strokes from attributes and style, clip paths as layer masks and text as text shapes, into one scene, one layer per top-level drawable, counting every other element and each reference cycle as skipped.

components.name: Symbols
components.description: Reusable symbol definitions and their instances on layers: how an instance maps the host timeline onto the symbol's own timeline, the add/remove/rename/convert-to-symbol commands, the instance add, remove, move and playback commands, and the check that rejects symbols that contain themselves.

components.name: State Machine
components.description: Interactive state machines: states that play a frame range of a scene, transitions fired by named triggers, typed bool/number inputs with transition conditions, the issues query that lists every broken rule and unreachable state without throwing, the format-layer check over it that FlareFormat.validate runs, the machine, state, transition and input commands, and the player that steps a machine at run time.

containers.name: CoreColor library
containers.description: Shared color module (Sources/CoreColor): color spaces and conversions for every app. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Color Spaces
components.description: Color3 and conversions between sRGB, linear sRGB, Display P3, XYZ D65 and OKLab through one shared transfer curve (public as TransferCurve, which CoreRaster's sRGB tone encoding uses); 8-bit display tables (DisplayTransfer: table decode and threshold encode for sRGB and Display P3); ColorError.

components.name: ICC Profiles
components.description: ColorProfile (an ICC matrix-and-curve profile: RGB or gray, colourants in XYZ D50 after Bradford adaptation, gamma, table and parametric curves) with the built-in sRGB, Display P3 and linear sRGB profiles, the bounds-checked ICC reader (v2 and v4 matrix-and-curve profiles; LUT-based, CMYK and Lab profiles and damaged bytes throw ColorError), and ProfileTransform between two profiles through the D50 PCS (source curves, colourants, Bradford adaptation between differing whites, inverse target colourants and curves; singular colourants throw ColorError). The ICC writer emits v4 bytes (header, tag table, 4-byte-aligned tags, mluc description, chad for RGB) that the reader reads back equal; a value that does not fit its field throws ColorError.

containers.name: CoreRaster library
containers.description: Shared raster module (Sources/CoreRaster): pixel buffers, compositing and image operations for Photo, Library and Halo. Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Pixel Buffer
components.description: PixelBuffer and RGBA: validated sizes, bounds-checked access, premultiply helpers; conversion to and from 8-bit sRGB or Display P3 display bytes through CoreColor's display tables, of the whole buffer or of one region without a crop copy; the tile grid for per-tile storage and paint, and TileDiff for tile-by-tile undo; RasterError.

components.name: Compositing
components.description: W3C blend modes and source-over compositing with opacity on premultiplied pixels, in place on the backdrop one row at a time (an opaque normal row at full opacity is copied in), with free functions that composite a copy. Compositing/ holds the W1 composites, such as compositing through a mask at its own offset.

components.name: Image Operations
components.description: Masks, resampling, crop, quarter turns and rotation by any angle with the straighten crop, blur, tone adjustments and histograms (levels, curves and histograms on linear or sRGB-encoded values) and cloning from an offset through a mask over PixelBuffer. W1/ declares the values the W1 engines share (AffineMatrix, ColorLUT, LayerEffect and the tone, matte, fill and gradient values), with no operations. Masks/ holds mask feathering, contours and mattes read from a buffer. Tone/ holds the color-family tone ops and the auto-tone suggestion. Effects/ holds the layer effects a PixelBuffer applies. Affine/ holds transforms through an AffineMatrix, flips and canvas padding. Fill/ holds flood fill by tolerance and raster gradient fills. Heal/ holds healing from sampled source pixels. Hash/ holds PerceptualHash, a 64-bit DCT hash of a buffer: resampled to 32 x 32 with the bilinear filter (which averages areas when shrinking), Rec. 709 luminance of the premultiplied values, so alpha composites over black, sRGB-encoded, a 2-D DCT-II, and one bit per coefficient (u, v) in 1...8 (the DC row and column dropped) set when it is above their median; distance is the popcount of the XOR, and the same buffer gives the same bits on every platform. It also holds DuplicateGroups, which puts ids whose hashes chain within a distance (clamped to 0...10, negative groups nothing, since past 10 random hashes start to chain) into groups of two or more, each id in one group, each group sorted by id and the list by first id, through a multi-index table over four 16-bit blocks and a union-find, near-linear in the number of hashes.

components.name: Layered Codecs
components.description: The neutral LayeredImage (pixel layers with offset, opacity, blend mode, visibility, clipping and a placed mask, nested groups, the merged composite) and CodecError; the PixelCodec protocol apps plug their PNG codec into, with RawPixelCodec as the lossless test stand-in (a PNG signature and IHDR, then raw components); ZipStore, the stored-only zip container; the bounds-checked ByteReader and PackBits; the PSD reader (8-bit RGB and grayscale, raw and RLE channels, layer masks, blend modes, nested groups, the merged image decoded as colour and one alpha only, within maxSide, maxLayers, maxDepth and maxTotalPixels); the OpenRaster reader (StackXML, a small bounded stack.xml parser, with layer PNGs sized from their IHDRs within maxSide and a summed maxTotalPixels before any is decoded through the PixelCodec); the PSD writer (8-bit RGB, every channel RLE, groups as divider records, masks, Unicode names, blend keys and the merged image, validated before any byte is written so PSD read reopens it equal); the OpenRaster writer (stack.xml, one PNG per layer through the PixelCodec, mergedimage.png, a thumbnail 256 on its longest side and app extra entries, validated before anything is encoded so OpenRaster read reopens it equal); PixelBuffer profile conversion (ProfileConvert: unpremultiply, source curve, matrix, target curve, alpha and alpha-0 pixels kept, no clamp, a non-finite result throws), its curve passes read from per-channel lookup tables (ProfileConvertCurves, linear interpolation checked against the exact curve when built, with values outside the tables taking the exact path).

containers.name: CoreAsset library
containers.description: Shared asset module (Sources/CoreAsset): the Asset and AssetRef model every app imports and exports, and its manifest.json codec. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Asset Model
components.description: Asset (id, kind, name, tags, version, source app, payload ref), AssetRef (id, version) and the manifest codec with size limits; AssetError.

components.name: Thumbnail Store
components.description: ThumbnailStore, the disk preview store: opaque encoded preview bytes (it never decodes images, and CoreAsset never imports CoreRaster) keyed by PreviewKey (asset, content token, SizeClass of 256, 1024 or 2560 px), each PreviewEntry naming its optional VolumeRef and relative path, and Availability (online, or offline with the volume). PreviewFiles is the layout: index.json, index.journal and p/<2 hex>/<16 hex>.bin files named by a 64-bit FNV-1a of the key, so no user text reaches a path; each file is FLPV, a version byte, a 4-byte big-endian length and that much JSON header naming its key, volume and path, then the payload. Every change runs under an exclusive flock on the folder's lock file and replaces a file by writing <name>.tmp whole, then renaming it over the old one. A write evicts the entry read longest ago (ties: the larger size class) while the payload bytes exceed the budget; opening a store never evicts. A read checks that the file's header names its key, returns nil and drops the entry when the file is gone, and bumps lastRead in memory; bumps are flushed with the next change, by the first read 2 s or more after the last flush, and on deinit, merged with the index on disk. PreviewJournal appends only the entries a change touched (FLPJ1:, the index's 16-hex generation, a newline, then one JSON put or drop per line); each store catches up on the lines others appended, ignores an unfinished last line and a journal of another generation, and compacts into a new snapshot past max(64, entries / 2) records, so index I/O per write is O(1) amortised. PreviewIndex is the snapshot codec (version 2; a version 1 index still loads) and its recovery: an index that fails to decode, names another version or an impossible size, or whose journal has a damaged line is renamed to index.damaged.json (its journal to index.damaged.journal, both kept) and rebuilt from the files: key, volume and path from each header, byteCount from the payload, lastRead from the modification date; a file whose header doesn't decode or that sits under another key's name is skipped and left on disk. Opening also deletes orphan .tmp files and drops entries whose file is gone. OfflineVolumes never probes the file system: the caller passes the mounted volume ids; entries(on:) matches by volume id alone, so a renamed volume keeps its entries; an entry whose volume id is not mounted reports offline while its bytes still read, and an entry with no volume is always online. Limits: the budget counts payloads only, not headers or the index; a negative budget throws; every failure is an AssetError; volume and duplicate facts beyond the entries belong to the catalog once its schema lands.

containers.name: CoreCatalog library
containers.description: Shared catalog module (Sources/CoreCatalog): photo and metadata catalog over SQLite, used by Library and the shared asset library. Linux-safe; depends only on GRDB.

components.name: Catalog Store
components.description: The catalog schema and its migrations, record types and queries (smart collection rules compiled to SQL) over a GRDB database; CatalogError, which GRDB's errors map to.

containers.name: CoreRender library
containers.description: Shared render module (Sources/CoreRender): the RenderBackend contract every app's Model draws through, its backends (a fake for tests, and the CPU backend over CoreRaster, the pixel reference), RenderDispatcher, which routes each op to a backend by support and health, the parity harness, and the Linux-safe parts of the Metal backend (capabilities, tiling math, cache keys). Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Render Contract
components.description: The RenderBackend contract: the op families (RenderOp), with the four CPU-first W1 families (maskedComposite, affine, effect, color) listed in RenderOp.notOnMetalYet, the one error type (RenderError), surface handles (RenderSurface), the tone adjustments the adjust and color families take (ToneAdjustment, whose family says which gates each case), the RenderBackend protocol with a not-on-this-backend default for each W1 method that throws unsupported with its family, the blend-mode-to-family and raster-error mappings every backend shares, the SurfaceStore that holds a backend's PixelBuffers behind one lock and updates one in place, and FakeBackend, the recording test double.

components.name: CPU Backend
components.description: CPUBackend, the CPU RenderBackend and pixel reference (Sources/CoreRender/CPU), supporting every op family: its surfaces are PixelBuffers held in the shared SurfaceStore; surface, read and release go through the SurfaceStore; display and composite (every blend mode, gated by its family) are the CoreRaster calls themselves, composite blending the stored backdrop in place under the store's lock so composites onto one surface apply one at a time, and crop, rotate, resample, blur, unsharp, each tone adjustment and masked clone (CPUBackend+Ops) each call the CoreRaster method they name and return a new surface. CoreRaster errors map to RenderError.raster with the same message. Each W1 family answers from its own file, CPUBackend+MaskedComposite, +Affine, +Effect and +Color (the color tone cases, reached from adjusted's switch): a stub that checks its surfaces under the family's gate and throws RenderError.unsupported(<family>) until its feature fills that file.

components.name: Render Dispatcher
components.description: RenderDispatcher, the routing between backends: each op goes to the preferred backend when it supports the op's family and is healthy, else to the CPU backend, recording the last fallback (op family and reason, unsupported or unhealthy). A surface made by the other backend is read and re-uploaded to the routed backend first, so a fallback never changes a pixel. Each W1 method routes by its own family: the masked composite by maskedComposite whatever its blend mode, transformed, flipped and the composite through a matrix by affine, applying by effect, and each tone adjustment by ToneAdjustment.family (adjust or color); the two W1 composites move a backdrop the way composite does.

components.name: Metal Support
components.description: The Metal backend's Linux-safe parts (Sources/CoreRender/Metal): binary16 half-float conversion for filling rgba16Float textures from Float32 buffers and reading them back; MetalCapabilities, the proven op set and health state that RenderDispatcher reads, with the families still compiling in the background held out of its effective supports and the CPU-first families in RenderOp.notOnMetalYet never enabled; SurfaceTiling, the 256 px tile grid a surface's textures follow, on CoreRaster's shared tile math, with the tiles a rect touches, the default memory budget (half the working set, at least one tile) and wholeImageFits, the overflow-checked whole-image buffer-limit check that blur, unsharp and retouch call (w x h x 16 bytes against the device's maxBufferLength); PipelineKey, the identity of one cached compute pipeline (op family plus a short identifier variant) and the kernel function name it maps to; DisplayTable, CoreColor's DisplayTransfer byte rules as Float thresholds (the curve's and the alpha's, plus CoreColor's own linear sRGB to Display P3 matrix, DisplayTransfer.p3FromLinearSRGB, as Float) that the Metal display kernel uploads, with encode, the kernel's per-pixel rule in Swift, outputFits, display's check against the device's buffer limit, and the CPU backend's error for a non-display space; and TileMap, the pixel map of a crop or quarter turn between two tilings (crop rectangles checked with CoreRaster's messages) split into tile-to-tile copy pieces, refusing a tiling of another size than the source it was made for; and CompositeMap, the overlap of a source placed on a backdrop at an integer offset (CoreRaster's in-place composite clip, safe for any Int offset) split into tile-to-tile pieces, with CoreRaster's opacity check; and ResampleTable, one resample axis's taps (CoreRaster's public ResampleFilter.taps, clamp-to-edge indices and weights normalised in Double, flattened and stored as Float, the identity for an unchanged length) as flat arrays the Metal resample kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's sum in Swift, and peakPixels, the largest buffer a resample allocates, checked against the device limit; and AdjustTable, every tone adjustment as CoreRaster's own adjustment on a probe line run through the CPU backend (per-channel gains for exposure and white balance, a square-root-spaced table over 0...1 with octave tables of the CPU's values outside it, 2^-24 to 2^40 on each side, read by exponent bits and interpolated on the mantissa, an overflowing octave holding the largest finite Float, for levels, curves and contrast, or a gain per Rec. 709 luminance, constant outside 0...1, for highlights/shadows) that the Metal adjust kernel uploads, with apply and map, the kernel's rule in Swift, and unsupported(.color) for every W1 colour case; and OpaqueRows, CoreRaster's opaque-row copy rule (.normal at opacity exactly 1, every stored alpha of the row exactly 1) as per-row flags of a composite piece split into maximal blit and kernel row runs; and BlurTable, CoreRaster's Gaussian blur kernel mirrored exactly (2 ceil(3 sigma) + 1 weights normalised in Double, stored as Float, sigma 0 the single weight 1, CoreRaster's sigma checks and messages, every weight pinned by test to CoreRaster's blur of an impulse) that the Metal blur kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's clamp-to-edge sum in Swift; and UnsharpRule, the amount and threshold the Metal unsharp kernel uploads (as two Floats), with CoreRaster's amount, threshold and overflow checks and messages, and apply, the kernel's own Float32 rule per premultiplied component (a difference from the blur strictly over Float(threshold) moves it by amount times the difference, one fused multiply-add), which agrees with CoreRaster's Double rule to Float rounding, a difference that close to the threshold taking either branch. Pure Swift integer and floating-point math, no Metal import, so it builds, tests and mutates on Linux.

components.name: Parity Harness
components.description: How one RenderBackend is measured against another (Sources/CoreRender/Parity): ParityTolerance (byte and linear bounds, .standard and .nonSeparable); ParityHarness.compare, which checks two results' sRGB display bytes through CoreRaster's rgba8 and their linear premultiplied Floats over visible pixels and names the worst pixel; ParityHarness.compare(golden:), the bytes-only compare of a result against a golden, encoded in the golden's color space (both compares count only alpha where both alpha bytes are 0); ParityPack, the layout of the packed CPU goldens (ParityPack.all, each sample's band of rows) and ParityGolden.band(from:op:sample:) and rows(_:), which copy one sample's golden out of its pack; the deterministic sample set per RenderOp (seeded buffers plus alpha 0, subnormal alpha, opaque rows and sources off every edge) and rendering a sample on any backend, with one Samples+<Family>.swift file per W1 family (masked composite, affine, effect, color) giving that family's samples and packs, all empty until its feature fills them; and golden files (raw rgba8 bytes beside a JSON header), validated as untrusted input.

containers.name: CoreRenderMetal library
containers.description: Metal render module (Sources/CoreRenderMetal): the Metal RenderBackend, macOS only. The one module allowed to import Metal; every file is wrapped in #if canImport(Metal), so Linux builds it empty.

components.name: Metal Backend
components.description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Normal composite (MB-4, enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device only) runs the composite_normal kernel in place on the backdrop's tiles, piece by piece from CompositeMap, with CoreRaster's sourceOver rule, opacity check and clip (an evicted backdrop tile is brought back to a texture first and the budget enforced after; a source that is the backdrop is read from a snapshot). The eleven other separable modes (MB-5) run as variants of the same in-place path, one blendSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's blend formula, with .blendSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-6). Hue, saturation, color and luminosity (MB-9) run through the same in-place path as one blendNonSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's Lum, Sat, SetLum, SetSat and ClipColor, with .blendNonSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-10). The opaque-row fast path (MB-6): under .normal at opacity exactly 1, the rows of a piece whose stored Float16 source alphas are all exactly 1 (read from the source tile, resident or staged) are copied onto the backdrop tile with blits instead of the kernel, split by OpaqueRows, with pixels equal to the CPU backend's copy. Resample (MB-8) runs bilinear and lanczos3 on the GPU as two separable passes of ResampleTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's pass order (the source read like `read`, resident tiles merged with shadows, and uploaded from the CPU), scattered into a new surface with components clamped to the finite half range; an invalid size throws the CPU backend's error, and a valid size whose largest buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength throws unsupported(.resample) with the backend still healthy, so the caller resamples on the CPU backend. Adjust (MB-13, MB-14; .adjust enabled at init) runs every tone adjustment (exposure, levels, curves, white balance, contrast, highlights/shadows) through the adjust_tone kernel tile by tile into a new surface, reading AdjustTable's per-channel gains, per-channel table with its two octave tables or luminance gain table on unpremultiplied values with CoreRaster's alpha guard (an evicted source tile through a temporary texture) and the CPU backend's errors for invalid parameters. Gaussian blur (MB-11) runs as two separable blur_pass passes of BlurTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's order (across, then down) with clamp-to-edge taps, scattered into a new surface by the resample scatter kernel; sigma 0 returns the pixels unchanged and an invalid sigma throws the CPU backend's error. Unsharp mask (MB-12) runs in one command buffer as blur_pass across the rows and then blur_unsharp, which finishes the blur down the columns and sharpens each premultiplied component in Float32 with UnsharpRule's parameters (the rule UnsharpRule.apply mirrors), scattered into a new surface; invalid parameters and an overflowing result throw the CPU backend's errors; .blur is enabled at init, and blur and unsharp throw unsupported while the backend is unhealthy and, with the backend still healthy, for a valid image whose whole-image buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength, so the caller runs them on the CPU backend. Clone through a mask (MB-15; .retouch enabled at init) packs the source, read like `read`, and the mask's coverage into whole-image buffers and runs retouch_clone into each tile of a new surface with CoreRaster's clone rule, the CPU backend's errors in its order, and offsets whose sources are all off the image returning the pixels unchanged; an image over maxBufferLength throws unsupported, and so does clone while the backend is unhealthy. Every family is enabled at init: display, transform, resample, adjust, blur and retouch on any device, and composite, blendSeparable and blendNonSeparable on a read-write tier 2 device only (elsewhere those modes throw unsupported). While the backend is unhealthy supports is empty and every op throws unsupported(<family>); with it healthy, display, resample, blur (gaussianBlur and unsharpMask) and retouch (cloned) throw unsupported(<family>) for a buffer over the device's maxBufferLength, leaving the backend healthy, so the caller runs the op on the CPU backend. A backend made with startingInBackground (MB-17) returns at once with every family it enables held in MetalCapabilities.compiling, so supports lacks them and their ops throw unsupported, and builds their built-in pipelines on a dispatch queue off the caller's, with the lock free, memoising each without replacing one already compiled on first use and releasing each family when done; a failed compile marks the backend failed and releases the family. The plain init compiles each pipeline on first use, under the lock.

systems.name: GRDB.swift
systems.description: External: SQLite toolkit for Swift (groue/GRDB.swift), pinned exact in Package.swift. Links the system SQLite; on Linux that needs libsqlite3-dev. Approved for CoreCatalog only.

relationships.description: shapes and layers are placed with Transform and Path
keyframe tracks carry easing; commands keep keyframes sorted
samples layer properties at a frame
writes transforms as matrices and shapes as paths
reads scenes, layers, shapes and fills
builds scenes, layers, shapes and fills
symbols hold layers and change the document through commands
states play frame ranges of a document's scenes; validated by FlareFormat
pixels carry colors in CoreColor's spaces
opens databases, runs migrations and queries through GRDB
backends hold surfaces as CoreRaster pixel buffers and the parity harness compares them; the CPU backend draws through CoreRaster's operations
display encodes into CoreColor's color spaces
implements the RenderBackend contract, measured against the CPU backend as it lands
